name: Structured Writing Support
title: Structured Writing Support
answer: Structured writing support means teaching students to use AI at specific stages of writing, such as organizing ideas before writing or getting feedback on a draft, while they do the writing themselves. It matters because writing is hard for many students with learning disabilities, and structured use may improve performance and confidence, but the IEP team must decide whether AI is an appropriate accommodation or skips skills the student needs to build.

sections.body: Structured writing support is teaching students to use AI at specific stages of writing rather than giving them a tool and leaving them alone. Writing is hard for many students with learning disabilities, and AI raises both hope and concern. The approach solves the problem of unstructured AI use by setting boundaries for each assignment through the AI use levels from Chapter 3. It aims to help students improve their writing while still doing the writing themselves. The text presents it as a way to support performance and confidence, especially for students with learning difficulties.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The text describes structured instruction at specific stages of writing, not handing over a tool. For school age students, that might mean using AI to organize ideas before writing, or to get feedback on a draft, while doing the writing themselves. The AI use levels from Chapter 3 help set the boundaries for each assignment. The IEP team should decide how AI fits a student's writing goals. The text does not give separate grade bands beyond school age students and the university students in the study.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text reports one study: Papanastasiou et al., 2026. In it, students in a teacher education program, including some with learning disabilities, received structured instruction in using AI to support their writing. Their writing improved, and students with learning difficulties gained the most in performance and confidence. The text notes the study involved university students, and similar research in schools has not yet been found.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets limits around structure and judgment. Students should not be handed a tool and left alone, and for school age students AI might organize ideas before writing or give feedback on a draft while the student does the writing. The AI use levels from Chapter 3 help set boundaries for each assignment. The IEP team decides how AI fits a student's writing goals, because for some students AI support may be an appropriate accommodation that lets them show what they know, while for others it may skip the very skills they need to build. That decision belongs to the team, based on the student's goals.
